headline.purpose: WinUI settings and feature page titles.

motion.name: state-standard
motion.purpose: State changes only; no page-load choreography. Honor prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Guest breadcrumb
components.description: Path strip on guest browse — Mist Header, 8px radius, System Blue links.
components.html: Root/share
components.css: .ds-breadcrumb { margin: 1.25rem 0; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; background: #eef1f6; border: 1px solid #d7dde5; border-radius: 8px; font-family: "Segoe UI Variable", "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-breadcrumb a { color: #0b57d0; text-decoration: none; } .ds-breadcrumb a:hover { text-decoration: underline; } .ds-breadcrumb a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0b57d0; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-split { margin: 0 0.35rem; color: #5c6570; }

components.name: Guest table wrap
components.description: Flat bordered file listing container — Card White, 10px radius, no shadow.
components.css: .ds-table-wrap { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #d7dde5; border-radius: 10px; overflow: auto; padding: 0.5rem; font-family: "Segoe UI Variable", "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif; color: #1b1f24; } .ds-file-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; } .ds-file-table th, .ds-file-table td { padding: 0.55rem 0.65rem; border-bottom: 1px solid #d7dde5; text-align: left; } .ds-file-table th { font-size: 0.85rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: #5c6570; } .ds-file-table tbody tr:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, #0b57d0 8%, transparent); } .ds-file-table a { color: #0b57d0; text-decoration: none; } .ds-file-table a:hover { text-decoration: underline; } .ds-file-table a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0b57d0; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-size { text-align: right; }

components.name: Guest link
components.description: Primary interactive text on guest web — System Blue, underline on hover.
components.css: .ds-link { color: #0b57d0; text-decoration: none; font-family: "Segoe UI Variable", "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-link:hover { text-decoration: underline; } .ds-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0b57d0; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Slot status
components.description: Upload-slot truth — Slot Green or Slot Red, never decorative.
components.html: 2 of 4 upload slots available.
components.css: .ds-slots { font-family: "Segoe UI Variable", "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif; color: #5c6570; margin: 0.25rem 0; } .ds-ok { color: #0f7b3a; font-weight: 600; } .ds-bad { color: #b42318; font-weight: 600; }

components.name: WinUI status line
components.description: Connection / mesh status — SemiBold title weight, louder than chrome.
components.css: .ds-status { margin: 0; font-family: "Segoe UI Variable", "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1.125rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.35; color: #1b1f24; }

components.description: Content page rhythm — 16px margin, calm unshadowed panel over Mica shell.

narrative.overview:
FAP’s visual system is a status-first mesh console: restrained Fluent utility with readable density and chrome that never outranks connection, peers, or transfers. The desktop client is the primary surface — WinUI 3, Mica shell, NavigationView — patterned after Microsoft PowerToys Settings. Guest web is a thin share desk: cool neutrals, one system blue for links, semantic greens/reds for slot state, and a capable directory table — not a second full client.

Personality is fast, plain, capable. One Segoe family carries everything. Accent color marks actions, selection, and state — never decoration. Depth is a Fluent hybrid: shell materials and system elevation on desktop; flat bordered panels and tonal steps on guest web.

This system explicitly rejects legacy dense P2P clients — cluttered toolbars, tiny fonts, every control visible at once — and rejects consumer “drive” marketing chrome.
keyCharacteristics: PowerToys Settings structure on desktop; thin guest table on web
Cool Fluent neutrals + System Blue accent ≤10%
Flat guest surfaces; Mica/shell depth only where the OS provides it
WCAG 2.2 AA target on guest web; automation-friendly WinUI

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: System Blue (and OS accent on desktop) is used for interactive affordances and selection only — ≤10% of any screen. Neutrals carry the rest.

rules.name: The Slot Signal Rule
rules.body: Green and red mean upload-slot / transfer truth, never decorative badges or marketing highlights.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Never introduce a second typeface for UI labels, buttons, or data. Segoe (or Fluent theme fonts) only.

rules.name: The Fixed Scale Rule
rules.body: Product UI uses fixed rem/px steps, not clamp() display sizes that shrink awkwardly in panes.

rules.name: The Flat Guest Rule
rules.body: Guest surfaces stay flat at rest. If a panel needs separation, use border + surface step, not box-shadow with blur ≥16px.

rules.name: The Shell Depth Rule
rules.body: Real depth belongs to the OS shell (Mica, NavigationView, TitleBar). Content pages stay calm and unshadowed.

dos: Do keep connection, peer, and transfer status visually louder than decorative chrome.
Do pattern desktop settings and nav after PowerToys Settings (microsoft/PowerToys src/settings-ui).
Do keep guest web thin: directory listing, breadcrumb, slot truth, download handoff.
Do use Cool Paper / Mist Header / Card White tonal steps and 1px Border Cool for structure on guest web.
Do meet WCAG 2.2 AA for guest text/contrast; keep WinUI AutomationIds and keyboard paths intact.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion on web and system motion settings on desktop.
donts: Don't recreate legacy dense P2P clients: cluttered toolbars, tiny fonts, every control visible at once.
Don't turn guest web into a second full client or a consumer cloud-drive marketing page.
Don't invent custom decorative shadows, glass stacks, or neon/RGB accents.
Don't use a second display typeface or File Explorer–style chrome as the product metaphor.
Don't spend System Blue / Slot Green / Slot Red on inactive decoration — they are interactive and semantic only.
Don't pair 1px borders with soft wide drop shadows (ghost-card) on guest panels.
